div.head: VIII Atr 41
div.ab: Gif munuc oððe mæssepreost wiðersaca wurðe mid ealle, he sy amansumod æfre, buton he þe rædlicor gebuge to his þearfe.
Gif munuc oððe mæssepreost wiðersaca wurðe mid ealle, he sy amansumod æfre, buton he þe rædlicor gebuge to his þearfe.
Gif munuc oððe mæssepreost wiðersaca wurðe mid ealle, he sy amansumod æfre, buton he þe rædlicor gebuge to his þearfe.
Wenn ein Mönch oder ein Priester gänzlich ein Abtrünniger wird, so werde er für immer excommunicirt, ausser wenn er um so bewusster sich dem, was ihm noth thut, unterwirft.
If a monk or a priest becomes a complete apostate, let him be excommunicated for ever, unless he submits all the more readily to what he needs to do.
If a monk or a priest becomes an utter apostate, he shall be excommunicated for ever, unless he is wise enough to return to his duty.
And if a monk or a mass-priest becomes altogether an apostate, he is ever to be excommunicated, unless he more sensibly return to his duty.
If a monk or a priest turns entirely to apostasy, he is to be excommunicated forever, unless he resumes his duty with greater prudence.

note.seg: Vielleicht benutzt durch II Cn 4, 1, der aber Abtrünnige (s. d. Gl; Exkommunikation 11) austreibt.—Vgl. Wb wiðersaca, wofür auch Toller 1252 die Bed. apostata belegt. Vermutlich sind nur die bewusst und fortgesetzt die Pflicht der Weihe bzw. Regel Ablehnenden gemeint, nicht Ketzer; s. d. Gl; Geistliche 22

Perhaps used by II Cn 4, 1, which, however, expels apostates (see that word in Gl; Exkommunikation 11).—Cf. Wb wiðersaca, for which Toller 1252 also attests the meaning apostata. Presumably only those are meant who knowingly and persistently reject the duty of their orders or of their rule respectively, not heretics; see that word in Gl; Geistliche 22
